claude-haiku-4.5.reason: formats formulas in Unicode subscripts; frozen deterministic extractor does not parse them, so in-loop detection recall ~0 -> no correction fires. Detection-limited, exactly the paper's two-stage thesis: repair cannot help where detection does not reach.

gpt-5.4-mini.reason: ASCII formatting -> detectable -> small, non-significant lift consistent with its moderate baseline error.

interpretation: Small closed models do NOT cleanly show the open-weights lift pattern. The axis is NOT simply capability tier: haiku (small closed) has high error but is undetectable due to formatting; gpt-5.4-mini (small closed) shows only marginal n.s. lift. The lift remains governed by DETECTION RECALL (formatting/extractability) x baseline error, not by open/closed or capability tier per se. This REFINES rather than overturns the openness observation: the operative variable is whether the verifier can extract the committed object, which interacts with model output formatting.
caveat: haiku subscript non-extraction is a real detection-recall limitation, disclosed; it is not a grading artifact (grade_record derives the formula and scores correctly).
